page: Google Cloud Platform ct5l-hightpu-8t is an accelerator-optimized machine type within the Cloud TPU lineup, designed specifically for machine learning model training and inference. The system couples a host configuration of 224 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs with 384 GB of system RAM, yielding approximately 1.71 GB of system memory per vCPU. For hardware acceleration, it integrates 8 Google TPU v5e chips that provide a collective pool of 128 GB of accelerator High Bandwidth Memory.

The compute profile is engineered around high accelerator density and dedicated host resources rather than general-purpose flexibility. Because the instance contains no local storage volumes, all storage pipelines must rely on external network-attached block storage or object storage buckets over the cloud network interface. Additionally, no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned to the instance, requiring private network topology or NAT configurations for internet-facing data transfers.

Cost efficiency for this instance type is characterized by its purpose-built TPU v5e architecture, which focuses on providing an optimal balance between execution performance and infrastructure expense for deep learning workloads compared to general-purpose GPUs. With eight TPU v5e chips running alongside a 224-vCPU host, the instance is intended for distributed deep learning training, large language model fine-tuning, high-throughput transformer inference, and data-intensive AI processing pipelines.
description: Google Cloud Platform ct5l-hightpu-8t is a specialized accelerator instance within the TPU family, tailored for machine learning and artificial intelligence tasks. The host system features 224 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs alongside 384 GB of system memory, providing approximately 1.71 GB of RAM per core. Compute workloads are powered by 8 Google TPU v5e accelerators supplying an aggregate 128 GB of accelerator memory. The instance does not include integrated local disk storage, necessitating the use of remote storage volumes or cloud object storage for data management, and includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses. With dense host computing capability and dedicated TPU hardware, this configuration provides cost-efficient acceleration for medium-to-large-scale deep learning model training, AI inference, and parallel neural network pipelines without the overhead of unused local disk arrays.
